label: JW · play
title: Jesus is the uncreated Creator (John 1:3 / Col 1:16)
text: "According to John 1:3, how many things came into existence without the Word?" (Answer: not one.)

label: JW · if they say
title: "'All' doesn't always mean all."
text: Here the verse defines it: "in the heavens and on the earth, visible and invisible, thrones, lordships" (Col 1:16). And John 1:3 says "not one thing."

label: JW · if they say
title: "He was Jehovah's master worker (Prov 8:30)."
text: Working alongside doesn't mean created. And Prov 8 personifies Wisdom (a "she"). Is God ever without wisdom?

label: JW · play
title: Jesus is Yahweh (the "First and Last" / Hebrews 1 chain)
text: "Who is the First and the Last in Isaiah 44:6?" (They'll say Jehovah.) "Does being the First and the Last mean you have a beginning?" (No.)

label: JW · if they say
title: "Jesus is the 'first and last' in a different sense."
text: "Then show me the text that makes the difference." Same title, same book, same speaker formula.

label: JW · if they say
title: "Hebrews 1:8 should say 'God is your throne.'"
text: v.8 opens "to the Son He says." The Father is speaking to the Son. And v.10 ("You, Lord…") has no throne issue at all.

label: JW · play
title: The Spirit is a Person and is Jehovah
text: "Does the Holy Spirit speak? Yes or no?" → Run the full 🔥 Holy Spirit Play. Best JW order: Acts 13:2 → Eph 4:30 → 2 Sam 23:2–3 + Acts 4:24–25. JW panels often go quiet at this point because they have no answer.

label: JW · play
title: Jesus is good, so He is God (Mark 10:18)
text: "Is Jesus good?" (They'll hesitate.)

label: JW · if they say
title: "He's not good like God"
text: "Name the moral flaw Jesus has that the Father doesn't."

label: JW · play
title: Watchtower prophecy test (use when they lean on the organization)
text: "Has the Watchtower ever announced a date in Jehovah's name that didn't happen?" "It was built in 1929. You know by who?" (Show a photo of Beth Sarim.)

label: JW · if they say
title: "We're not prophets, just students making calculations"
text: "Announcing future dates as God's truth is prophecy by definition."

label: JW · objection
title: "John 1:1 says 'a god.' No article = indefinite."
text: A predicate noun before the verb without the article describes nature (Colwell / qualitative). "The Word was God" in nature. "Is God 'a love'? Was John sent from 'a god'? Your NWT says 'God' in 1:6. Why not in 1:1?"

label: JW · objection
title: "Ton theon = the Almighty; theos = a lesser god."
text: That's just Greek case. Ton theon is accusative after pros; theos is nominative. Case endings aren't ranks. "Is the Father a lesser god when he's in the nominative?"

label: JW · objection
title: "Firstborn of creation" (Col 1:15) = first created
text: Prōtotokos = preeminent heir. v.16 gives the reason: "because by Him all things were created." "Who was Israel's first king? Saul. So how is David 'firstborn' of the kings?"

label: JW · objection
title: "Only-begotten" (John 3:16) = uniquely created
text: Monogenēs = one-of-a-kind / unique (Heb 11:17: Isaac wasn't Abraham's only son). "Was Isaac Abraham's only child?"

label: JW · objection
title: "Beginning of the creation of God" (Rev 3:14)
text: Archē = origin / ruler / source. He's where creation comes from. "If you're the originator of your business, aren't you its origin?"

label: JW · objection
title: "John 5:19: Jesus can do nothing on his own"
text: That shows the Persons are distinct and act together. Finish the verse: "whatever the Father does, the Son does likewise." "Does the Father do anything without the Son?"

label: JW · objection
title: "John 14:28: 'the Father is greater than I'"
text: Greater in role, in the Son's humbled human state. Not in nature. Phil 2:6–7. "Is a husband 'greater' in nature than his wife because he leads?"

label: JW · objection
title: "Psalm 8 / Heb 2: everything is subject to man, not Jesus"
text: Heb 2:9 identifies the "him": "namely Jesus." "Who are we going to trust, you or the author of Hebrews?"

label: JW · objection
title: "Daniel 7: Jesus wasn't seated / Rev 3:21: believers sit on the throne too"
text: Sharing kingdom authority ≠ sitting on high in heaven, the place that belongs to Yahweh alone (Ps 113:5). "Show me anyone other than Jesus who sits 'on high' at the right hand of the Majesty."

label: JW · objection
title: "Holy Spirit = active force"
text: → 🔥 Holy Spirit Play "Can a force be grieved?"

label: JW · objection
title: "Trinity isn't in the Bible."
text: Word–concept fallacy. "Jehovah's Witness" isn't in the Bible as a denomination name either. Is the concept taught? "Is the word 'theocracy' in the Bible?"

label: JW · objection
title: "Jesus is Michael the Archangel."
text: Scripture never says it. Michael did not dare rebuke Satan himself (Jude 9); Jesus commands him directly (Matt 4:10). God never called any angel "My Son," and all the angels worship the Son. "To which of the angels did God ever say, 'You are My Son'?"

label: JW · objection
title: "Jesus was raised as a spirit, not in a body."
text: He said a spirit does not have flesh and bones as He has, He showed His wounds, and He said He would raise His body. "In John 2:19–21, what did Jesus say He would raise?"

label: JW · objection
title: "Only 144,000 go to heaven."
text: Right after the 144,000, John sees a great multitude no one could count standing before the throne, serving God in His temple. "Where is the great multitude standing in Rev 7:9?"

label: JW · objection
title: "The dead are unconscious. The soul stops existing."
text: Paul expected to depart and be with Christ, away from the body and at home with the Lord. The souls under the altar speak. "How do the souls in Rev 6:10 cry out if they don't exist?"

label: JW · objection
title: "Hell isn't eternal. The wicked are simply destroyed."
text: Jesus uses the same word, "eternal," for the punishment and for the life in one sentence. "If the punishment isn't eternal, is the life?"

label: JW · objection
title: "Jesus died on a stake, not a cross."
text: Don't make this the fight. Thomas speaks of nails, plural, in His hands, and the sign was placed above His head. Then go back to who Jesus is. "Why 'nails,' plural, for His hands?"

label: JW · objection
title: "You must use God's name, Jehovah."
text: The apostles take the Old Testament "name" texts and apply them to Jesus. Joel's "call on the name of Yahweh" becomes confessing Jesus as Lord. "In Rom 10:13, whose name is in view, given verse 9?"

label: JW · objection
title: "Jesus is a god, a mighty one, but not the true God."
text: Jehovah says no god was formed before or after Him and He knows of no other. So is Jesus a true God or a false god? Thomas calls Him "my Lord and my God" and Jesus accepts it. "Is Jesus a true god or a false god?"

label: JW · objection
title: "People only did obeisance to Jesus, not worship."
text: All the angels worship the Son. Every creature gives the same honor to God and to the Lamb. An angel refuses it; Jesus receives it. "Why does the angel refuse what Jesus accepts?"

label: JW · objection
title: "You need Jehovah's organization to be saved."
text: Salvation is by grace through faith, not works, and not membership. When others left, Peter did not ask where to go, but to whom. "To whom did Peter say we should go?"

label: JW · quick card
title: John 1:3: "not one thing came into existence without Him" → "So did Jesus create Himself?"

label: JW · quick card
title: Col 1:16–17 (NWT): "all other things." The word "other" isn't in the Greek, and the Watchtower's own interlinear shows it.

label: JW · quick card
title: Isa 44:6 + Rev 1:17 / 22:13: First and Last → "Does being the First and Last mean you have a beginning?"

label: JW · quick card
title: Heb 1:10–12 + Ps 102:25–27: the Father addresses the Son with a Psalm spoken to Jehovah as Creator.

label: JW · quick card
title: Acts 13:2 + Heb 3:7–11: the Spirit says "me / I," and the Spirit is the one tested in the wilderness → see 🔥 Holy Spirit Play.

label: JW · quick card
title: Deut 18:21–22: the 1914 / 1925 predictions → the test of a prophet.

label: Unitarian · play
title: The Holy Spirit (lead with this)
text: "Does the Spirit have a mind? Yes or no?" → 🔥 Holy Spirit Play. Best order against Unitarians: "Does the Spirit have a mind? Yes or no?" → Acts 13:2 → Heb 3:7–11 → 2 Sam 23:2–3 / Acts 4:25 → Rom 8:9 ("Spirit of Christ").

label: Unitarian · play
title: The Angel of Yahweh claims to be God, with no "thus says the Lord"
text: "Can we be honest with the text: does the Angel of God claim to be the God of Bethel? Yes or no?"

label: Unitarian · if they say
title: "Agency: a messenger speaks in the first person for the king."
text: "Show me the 'thus says the Lord.'" There isn't one. "Without it, how do you know when a messenger is speaking for God or for himself?" Moses talking in his tent and Jonah running away weren't oracles just because they had the "messenger" title.

label: Unitarian · if they say
title: "Can't an ambassador speak as the king?"
text: Use their analogy: "Can the agent of the King claim to BE the King?" "Yahweh can send agents, but agents can't claim to be Yahweh, or they drop dead."

label: Unitarian · if they say
title: "Malak means a lesser being, sent by a superior."
text: Malak / angelos names a function, not a nature. John the Baptist and his disciples are called angelos (Mark 1:2; Luke 7:24). "Does the word itself tell you what kind of being the messenger is?" "If I send you with a message, am I superior to you in nature?"

label: Unitarian · play
title: Christ is the Yahweh of the Exodus (1 Cor 8:6 → 10:9)
text: "Who's the one Lord in 1 Corinthians 8?" (They'll say Jesus.) "In Numbers 21, who did Israel test, and who sent the serpents?" (They'll say Yahweh.)

label: Unitarian · if they say
title: "Textual variant: some manuscripts say 'the Lord'"
text: Fine. In this same letter, the "one Lord" is Jesus Christ (8:6). Either reading lands in the same place.

label: Unitarian · play
title: Real pre-existence (John 1:3, Col 1:16, Heb 1)
text: "Do you believe that the Word was created?" (They'll say yes. Then go to John 1:3.) "According to John 1:3, was anything made without the Word? Yes or no?" "Who is the author of life according to Acts 3:15?"

label: Unitarian · play
title: The Messiah shares Yahweh's nature (Zech 13:7)
text: "In Zechariah 13:7, who is the Shepherd that gets struck?" (Jesus says it's Him, Matt 26:31.)

label: Unitarian · objection
title: The syllogism: "YHWH is the Most High; Jesus is the Son of the Most High; if Jesus is YHWH, Jesus is his own Father."
text: Equivocation. You're treating "Yahweh" as naming only one person. It can name the nature or any one Person. Jesus is Yahweh by nature, not the person of the Father. "Is 'Judah' a person or a tribe?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "John 17:3: the Father is 'the only true God'"
text: Yes, the Father is the only true God. Trinitarians agree. "Only" excludes false gods, not the Son: the same John calls Jesus "the true God" (1 John 5:20). "Jude calls Jesus our 'only Lord.' Does that make the Father not Lord?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "1 Cor 8:6: one God, the Father"
text: Same verse: "one Lord, Jesus Christ." Paul splits the Shema (Deut 6:4) between Father and Son. If "one God, the Father" excludes Jesus from being God, "one Lord, Jesus" excludes the Father from being Lord. "Is the Father not Lord?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "God is not a man" (Num 23:19; Hos 11:9)
text: God is not a man by nature (who lies or changes). The Son took on a human nature (John 1:14) and stayed God. "Can the God who made human nature add it to Himself?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "Jesus died, and God can't die"
text: The Person of the Son died in His human nature. The divine nature doesn't die. Two natures, one Person. "Who was crucified in 1 Cor 2:8?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "Homoousios / Nicaea / the church invented it"
text: The term is a summary of biblical teaching, not new revelation. Answer from the text, not from church history. "Fine. Set Nicaea aside. Let's just read Rev 3:14 / John 1:3."

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "Archē (Rev 3:14) = first creature" / "Abba means source"
text: Archē = origin / ruler / active cause. The NT is Greek, not Hebrew, and Abba means "Father." "Does the software exist before you made it?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "Context limits 'Author of life' / 'all things'"
text: Make them show the verse that limits it. "Where in the chapter does it say that?" (then wait)

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "The Spirit is rational energy / information / a vibe"
text: → 🔥 Holy Spirit Play "Can energy be rational without personhood?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "Jesus has a God (John 20:17), so He isn't God."
text: As true man He has a God. The same chapter has Thomas call Him "my God," and Hebrews calls the Son "God" while speaking of "Your God." Both are true of the one Person. "In Heb 1:8–9, who is called God, and who is His God?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "Jesus didn't know the day or the hour (Mark 13:32)."
text: Two natures. As man He grew in wisdom; as God He knows all things. "How can Peter say, 'Lord, You know all things'?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "God cannot be tempted (James 1:13), but Jesus was."
text: He was tempted as man, from outside, and never sinned. That is the point of the incarnation: a true human High Priest. "Did the temptation ever find sin in Him?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "No one has ever seen God, but people saw Jesus."
text: Finish the verse: the only begotten God has explained Him. No one has seen the Father apart from the Son. And Isaiah saw Yahweh, and John says he saw Christ's glory. "Who did Isaiah see in the temple?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "Philippians 2 only says Jesus didn't grasp at being equal with God."
text: He was existing in the form of God and then took the form of a slave. You cannot take on humanity if you were only ever human. "When did He 'take' the form of a slave, if He was only ever a man?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "The 'Word' in John 1 is God's plan, not a person."
text: The Word is with God, makes all things, becomes flesh, and shares glory with the Father before the world existed. Plans don't do that. "Can a plan share glory with the Father before the world existed?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "'Before Abraham was, I am' just means He was foreordained."
text: His hearers understood Him. They picked up stones. Nobody is stoned for being part of God's plan. "Why did they try to stone Him?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "Thomas was only exclaiming in surprise (John 20:28)."
text: The text says Thomas said it to Him, and Jesus blesses the confession instead of rebuking it. "Does Jesus correct Thomas or commend him?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "Jesus is called 'god' the way judges and Moses were."
text: No judge is worshiped by angels, called Creator, or called the true God. And all are to honor the Son just as they honor the Father. "Is anyone told to honor Moses just as they honor the Father?"

label: Unitarian · objection
title: "Matthew 28:19 was added later."
text: Every Greek manuscript that contains the passage has the three-fold name, and Paul blesses in the same three-fold way. "Which manuscript leaves it out?"

label: Unitarian · quick card
title: Acts 13:2 → "Do actions have authority, or do persons?"

label: Unitarian · quick card
title: Heb 3:7–11 / Ps 95 → "Who's the 'Me' the Spirit says they tested?"

label: Unitarian · quick card
title: Gen 31:11–13 → the Angel of God says "I am the God of Bethel." "Where's the 'thus says the Lord'?"

label: Unitarian · quick card
title: 1 Cor 8:6 + 1 Cor 10:9 + Num 21:5–6 → "When was Christ put to the test with serpents?"

label: Unitarian · quick card
title: John 1:3 / Col 1:16 → "How were all things created through Him if He didn't exist yet?"

label: Unitarian · quick card
title: Isa 44:6 + Rev 1:17 → "So Yahweh has a beginning?"

label: Mormon · play
title: No gods before Him, no gods after Him (against exaltation)
text: "Can I read you something God says about Himself and get your take?"

label: Mormon · if they say
title: "1 Cor 15:40–41: celestial / terrestrial glories."
text: In context that's about kinds of resurrection bodies, compared to the sun, moon and stars. It's about glorified bodies, not becoming creator gods.

label: Mormon · if they say
title: "We're joint heirs with Christ (Rom 8:17)."
text: Yes, we inherit the kingdom. Inheriting the kingdom isn't becoming God.

label: Mormon · if they say
title: "We'll be like Him (1 John 3:2)."
text: Conformed to Christ's moral image with a glorified body. Not divine in nature.

label: Mormon · play
title: God has always been God (against "God was once a man")
text: "Can we agree that God in His nature has to be infinite, always existing?" (They'll say yes.) "Joseph Smith taught God was not always God, but became God. Is that hearsay or fact?" (Use when they bring up exaltation themselves.)

label: Mormon · if they say
title: "That's not official doctrine / just my thought"
text: King Follett discourse (Joseph Smith, 1844), "God himself was once as we are now." Then: "Whether it's official or not, if a teaching contradicts the eternal God, it's a false teaching."

label: Mormon · play
title: Three separate gods vs. one God (the "Godhead")
text: "So these are three separate gods, then?"

label: Mormon · if they say
title: "Jesus' baptism shows three separate beings."
text: It shows three distinct Persons. Distinct ≠ separate gods. One Being, three Persons.

label: Mormon · if they say
title: "Yahweh is the title of the Godhead council, like three judges sharing one court."
text: "If one judge steps out and says 'I am the court,' is that right?" But each Person is fully Yahweh, not a third of a committee. And Neh 9:6 says Yahweh alone created.

label: Mormon · if they say
title: "The Angel / Son is Yahweh only by agency."
text: "Can the agent of the King claim to be the King?"

label: Mormon · play
title: Phantom prophecy (Joseph Smith wrote himself into Genesis)
text: "Where can I read the prophecy about Joseph Smith in a text that Joseph Smith didn't produce?" "Why would God pick that person to re-reveal that prophecy?" (After you name JST Genesis 50:33 and 2 Nephi 3:15.)

label: Mormon · if they say
title: "Jesus read Himself into Isaiah too (Luke 4:21)"
text: "He's quoting a different prophet, from a public scroll. He didn't add new verses to Genesis."

label: Mormon · objection
title: "There was a Great Apostasy, so God restored the church through Joseph Smith."
text: Jesus promised the gates of hell would not prevail and that He'd be with His church always. "Did Jesus fail to keep His promise for 1,700 years?"

label: Mormon · objection
title: "Pray about the Book of Mormon and you'll feel a burning in the bosom."
text: Feelings test nothing. Scripture tells us to test by Scripture. The heart is deceitful. "If a Muslim feels a burning about the Quran, is it true too?"

label: Mormon · objection
title: "Ye are gods" (Ps 82:6 / John 10:34)
text: Ps 82 is about unjust human judges who "will die like men" (v.7). It's irony and judgment, not a promise of exaltation. "Do these 'gods' die?"

label: Mormon · objection
title: "The Father has a body of flesh and bone."
text: God is spirit, invisible, and fills heaven and earth. "Does a spirit have flesh and bones?" (Luke 24:39)

label: Mormon · objection
title: "Ezekiel 37's two sticks = Bible + Book of Mormon."
text: Read v.15–22: the sticks are Judah and Joseph/Ephraim, the divided kingdoms joined into one nation under one king. "What does v.22 say the two sticks become?"

label: Mormon · objection
title: "Jesus is 'a god'; the Father is 'the God.'"
text: Scripture never calls Jesus "a god." He is the God: Titus 2:13, John 20:28. "Show me 'a god' in John 1:1."

label: Mormon · objection
title: "Baptism for the dead" (1 Cor 15:29)
text: Paul says "they" (some group), not "we." It's an ad hominem for the resurrection, not a command. Heb 9:27. "Where is it ever commanded?"

label: Mormon · objection
title: "We are saved by grace after all we can do (2 Nephi 25:23)."
text: Scripture says grace through faith, not of works. God justifies the one who does not work but believes. Good works are the fruit, not the price. "Have you done all you can do?"

label: Mormon · objection
title: "The Bible is true only as far as it is translated correctly. Plain and precious things were lost."
text: God promised His word would stand forever. We have manuscripts more than a thousand years older than Joseph Smith, and none of them contain the "lost" material he added. "Which verse was lost, and which manuscript shows it?"

label: Mormon · objection
title: "We have a living prophet today."
text: In these last days God has spoken in His Son. Any prophet is tested by Scripture, and a different gospel is rejected even from an angel. "What happens to a prophet whose word contradicts Scripture?"

label: Mormon · objection
title: "Jesus and Lucifer are spirit brothers."
text: Jesus created all things in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible, including every angelic power. The Creator is not the brother of His creature. "If Jesus made everything invisible in heaven, who made Lucifer?"

label: Mormon · objection
title: "We all lived as spirits with God before we were born."
text: God forms the spirit of man within him. Only Christ is "from above." "Who does Jesus say is from above, and who is from below?"

label: Mormon · objection
title: "The priesthood was restored through Joseph Smith."
text: The Aaronic priesthood was set aside, and Jesus holds His priesthood permanently. Every believer is already part of a royal priesthood. "If Jesus holds it permanently, who else needs to?"

label: Mormon · objection
title: "Families are forever through temple marriage."
text: Jesus says that in the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage. The temple veil was torn, and God does not dwell in temples made with hands. "What did Jesus say about marriage in the resurrection?"

label: Mormon · objection
title: "There are three degrees of glory. Almost everyone is saved somewhere."
text: Jesus speaks of two roads and two ends: eternal punishment or eternal life. "How many destinations does Jesus name?"

label: Mormon · objection
title: "We're Christians too. We believe in Jesus."
text: Be gentle here. Paul warns of "another Jesus." The question is which Jesus: the eternal God who made all things, or a created spirit who became a god. "Is the Jesus you trust the eternal Creator, or a being who became a god?"

label: Mormon · objection
title: "James 1:5: ask God, and He will tell you it's true."
text: James is about wisdom in trials, not a test for new scripture. The Bereans were praised for checking everything against the Scriptures. "What did the Bereans check Paul against?"

label: Mormon · quick card
title: Isa 44:6, 8: "besides me there is no God… Is there a God besides me? There is no Rock; I know not any."

label: Mormon · quick card
title: Isa 43:10: "Before me no god was formed, nor shall there be any after me." "So how can there be gods after Him?"

label: Mormon · quick card
title: Ps 90:2: "from everlasting to everlasting You are God." "When was God not God?"

label: Mormon · quick card
title: Alma 11:28–29 (BoM): "Is there more than one God? … No."

label: Mormon · quick card
title: Moroni 8:18 (BoM): God is "unchangeable from all eternity to all eternity."

label: Mormon · quick card
title: John 1:1: "the Word was God," not "a god."

label: Muslim · play
title: THE ISLAMIC DILEMMA (run it in phases)
text: "Does the Quran say the Torah and the Gospel came from Allah? Yes or no?" The Quran says the Torah and Gospel in Christians' and Jews' hands in the 7th century were God's word and confirmed them. We have the 7th-century Bible (and far older manuscripts: Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, Dead Sea Scrolls). That Bible says Jesus is the Son of God, died and rose. Either the Bible is reliable, and it contradicts the Quran → Islam is false. Or the Bible is corrupted, and then the Quran confirmed a corrupted book → Islam is false. Either way, Islam fails.

label: Muslim · if they say
title: "It only confirms the original revelation, not what they had."
text: "Read it again: 'that which is with you.' Is there any part of the verse that says it's only confirming part, some, or a piece?"

label: Muslim · if they say
title: "It's general confirmation. It retells the stories and edits out the errors."
text: "Define 'confirm.'" (= verify as true). Then Q 2:85: "Does Allah allow people to believe some of the Scripture and reject the rest?" "Give me one verse that says the Quran only confirms part."

label: Muslim · if they say
title: "Q 2:79: woe to those who write the book with their own hands."
text: That condemns people making counterfeit books. It doesn't say the real Scripture was changed. "If I wrote a book with my own hands and said it's from God, does that mean the Quran is now corrupted?"

label: Muslim · if they say
title: "Q 5:13: they distort words from their places."
text: Distorting meaning / misquoting ≠ the text is lost. The same chapter tells them to judge by what they have (5:43, 47). And Q 6:115: "None can change His words."

label: Muslim · if they say
title: "Having it is like having $100. You can still lose it."
text: The texts are present tense: they literally brought out the scroll.

label: Muslim · if they say
title: "The Bible is corrupted" (said only after a verse goes against them)
text: "You brought me the Bible as a source to prove Muhammad. When we read it, it's suddenly corrupted?"

label: Muslim · if they say
title: They pivot to "Is Jesus God?" or "the Trinity is 3 gods."
text: "You're not going to 'is Jesus God' your way out of this. Defend the Quran first."

label: Muslim · play
title: Muhammad isn't in the Bible (the John 14 and Q 61:6 claims)
text: "So where does Jesus mention Muhammad?" "So the Comforter here, you believe that's Muhammad?" (Once they cite John 14.)

label: Muslim · play
title: Only God gives eternal life
text: "Who gives eternal life?" (God.)

label: Muslim · play
title: Son vs. servant
text: "Is Jesus the son of Allah?" (They'll say no.) "Where in the Bible does it say the Son of God is just a servant?" (When they say "son" only means servant.)

label: Muslim · play
title: Tawhid consistency (the Black Stone)
text: "Can the Black Stone benefit you or harm you? Yes or no?" "Why are people rubbing oil on this rock that doesn't do anything for you?"

label: Muslim · play
title: Moral problems (only if they claim Islam is morally superior)
text: "You say Islam is morally superior. Can we read a few verses of the Quran and see?" "It talks about the women that you're allowed to have, right?" (On Q 4:24.)

label: Muslim · objection
title: "How can God be 3 and 1?"
text: Three in one sense (Persons), one in another (Being). Different categories, no contradiction. Hold up the Hafs, Warsh and Qalun Qurans: "How many Qurans am I holding? These three are one?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "Jesus never said 'I am God, worship me.'"
text: He said things only God could say, and accepted what only God receives. Watch for the goalpost shift. "First you wanted a verse. Now it has to come from Jesus' mouth?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "God is not a man" (Hosea 11:9)
text: Correct by nature. The Son added a human nature. Two natures, one Person. And don't let them skip the verse you gave first. "Do you acknowledge Heb 1:3 says the Son is the exact imprint of God's nature?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "Which God sent Jesus? Who was He praying to?"
text: One God, three Persons. The Father sent the Son. Jesus prayed as a true man. "In John 17:5 Jesus asks for the glory He had with the Father before the world existed. Can a mere prophet pray that?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "Jesus wasn't crucified" (Q 4:157)
text: Every early source, Christian and non-Christian (Josephus c. AD 93, Tacitus c. AD 116), agrees He was crucified. The Quran denies it 600 years later with no source. And the Injil the Quran confirms teaches it. "Who did Allah make look like Jesus, and did he deceive the disciples into starting Christianity?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "Paul corrupted Jesus' message."
text: Paul's gospel was checked and approved by Peter, James and John. And Q 61:14 praises Jesus' disciples as Allah's helpers, who won. "Q 61:14 says Allah made Jesus' followers victorious. The faith that won taught what Paul taught. Did Allah back the wrong side?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "The Torah is one book, but you have five."
text: The Torah = Genesis to Deuteronomy, the five books of Moses: one Torah in five scrolls. Jewish tradition says Joshua added the account of Moses' death (Deut 34). "The Quran has 114 surahs. Is it 114 books, or one?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "The Trinity is pagan / Allah is 'the third of three'"
text: The Quran pictures worship of God, Jesus and Mary (Q 5:116; cf. Q 5:73–75). That is not the Trinity Christians believe: one God in three Persons, Father, Son and Holy Spirit. "Which Christian ever taught Mary is part of the Trinity?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "Jesus ate, slept and prayed. God doesn't do that."
text: He is truly God and truly man. The Word became flesh. Hunger and sleep belong to His human nature; they don't cancel His divine nature. "If God chose to enter His creation as a man, who could stop Him?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "The Injil was one book given to Jesus. You have four, written by men."
text: "Gospel" means the good news about Jesus. And the Quran tells the people of the Gospel to judge by what they had in the 7th century, which was these four. "What Gospel did Christians have in Muhammad's day?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "Jesus was sent only to the lost sheep of Israel."
text: His earthly ministry went to Israel first, as promised. Then He sent His disciples to all nations, as Isaiah foretold. "Who does Jesus send them to in Matt 28:19?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "The Bible has contradictions and too many versions."
text: Translations are not different Bibles. The manuscript differences are known and printed in the footnotes, and no teaching depends on them. Ask for one and read it together. "Which contradiction? Let's read it."

label: Muslim · objection
title: "God can simply forgive. He doesn't need a sacrifice."
text: A judge who lets the guilty go is unjust. God will by no means leave the guilty unpunished. At the cross He is both just and the justifier. Even the Quran ransoms Abraham's son with a great sacrifice. "If a judge lets the guilty go free, is he a just judge?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "No one can carry another person's sins (Q 6:164)."
text: The Torah the Quran confirms is built on substitution: the sins of the people laid on another. Isaiah foretold One who would bear the iniquity of us all. "What does Isaiah 53:6 say Yahweh laid on Him?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "Jesus and His disciples were Muslims."
text: His disciples worshiped Him, called Him Lord and God, and preached that He was crucified and raised. "Would a Muslim say 'My Lord and my God' to Jesus?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "Muhammad is named in Song of Songs 5:16."
text: The Hebrew word there is an ordinary word for "desirable," used by a bride about her beloved. The same word family describes Ezekiel's wife and children in Hosea. "Is Muhammad also in Ezekiel 24:16, where the same word is used?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "Islam is the fastest-growing religion, so it must be true."
text: Truth isn't a headcount. Jesus said the many take the wide road. "Is something true because many people believe it?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "The Quran is a miracle. No one can produce a chapter like it."
text: That test has no judge and no standard. The Quran gives a better test: check with those who read the Scripture before. "Who judges the contest, and by what standard?"

label: Muslim · objection
title: "Jesus said, 'Why do you call Me good? Only God is good.'"
text: He didn't say He isn't good. He asked the man why he said it. Jesus calls Himself the Good Shepherd. "Is Jesus good?"

label: Muslim · quick card
title: Q 5:47: "Let the people of the Gospel judge by what Allah has revealed therein."

label: Muslim · quick card
title: Q 5:43: "How do they come to you for judgment while they have the Torah, in which is the judgment of Allah?"

label: Muslim · quick card
title: Q 2:41: "Believe in what I have sent down, confirming that which is with you."

label: Muslim · quick card
title: Q 2:85: "Do you believe in part of the Scripture and disbelieve in part?"

label: Muslim · quick card
title: John 14:16–17: the Helper "dwells with you and will be in you." "Was Muhammad living with the disciples?"

label: Atheist · play
title: Pin down the position
text: "Are you claiming God doesn't exist, or that you don't know?"

label: Atheist · if they say
title: "I just believe in one less god than you."
text: "Rejecting false gods because of the evidence is exactly what I'm asking you to do with the true one. Follow the evidence."

label: Atheist · play
title: Design + life from life
text: "Have you ever seen something this ordered come from something non-intelligent?"

label: Atheist · play
title: The "borrowed capital" questions (Reformed / presuppositional)
text: "Can I ask you about three things we both rely on every day: logic, right and wrong, and your own reasoning?" "Where do you get this idea of bad from?" (When they call something evil or unfair.)

label: Atheist · play
title: The Resurrection (the center)
text: "If Jesus really rose from the dead, would you become a Christian?" "What about the people who didn't believe in Jesus, persecuted His followers, then said, 'I saw Jesus'?" (When they say it's a game of telephone.)

label: Atheist · objection
title: "Jesus is a copy of Horus / Osiris / Mithras."
text: Comes from pop media (Zeitgeist, Religulous), not the Egyptian sources. No virgin birth, no crucifixion, no resurrection in the primary texts. "Which primary Egyptian text says Horus was born of a virgin? Name it."

label: Atheist · objection
title: "It's like the Salem witch trials / a game of telephone."
text: Public execution under Pilate, guarded tomb, and eyewitnesses who were still alive when it was written (1 Cor 15:6, "most are still alive"). "Who dies for what they know is a lie?"

label: Atheist · objection
title: "Why do babies get cancer because Adam ate fruit?"
text: Federal headship. A head affects those he represents, like a mother's toxins affecting her unborn child. Adam's fall broke creation. Christ, the second Adam, restores it. "If God exists, wouldn't you expect Him to fix the fall? He did, in Christ."

label: Atheist · objection
title: "If God knew I'd reject Him, why create me? That's unjust."
text: God is just and owes no one mercy. No one is forced to reject Him: people reject Him because they love their sin, and they are responsible for it. Hell is the just penalty for real guilt, not a mistake. Yet God freely offers Christ to all who come, and no one who comes is turned away. "Is there anything you've done that a perfectly just judge should ignore?"

label: Atheist · objection
title: "A jealous God who demands worship is vain."
text: Not all jealousy is sinful. A husband who's jealous over an unfaithful wife is rightly jealous. God made every breath you take, so He has a rightful claim. "If your wife slept with another man, would your jealousy be ugly, or just?"

label: Atheist · objection
title: "Heaven/hell is a game show: pick a door."
text: It's not a game show. It's a command and an invitation. God commands everyone to repent and offers Himself, the greatest good. Whoever refuses Him is responsible for that refusal. "It's not God playing games. You're playing games with Him."

label: Atheist · objection
title: "So many religions. How would I know which one?"
text: Follow the evidence step by step: (1) there's a Source of life → (2) which claim about that Source is historically testable? Only Christianity rests on a public resurrection. "Which other religion stakes everything on a public event you can investigate?"

label: Atheist · objection
title: "Who created God?"
text: The question assumes everything needs a cause. It doesn't. Only what begins to exist needs a cause. God never began; He is uncaused by definition, the cause of everything outside Himself. Asking who made Him is a category mistake, like asking who made the One who was never made. "Does everything need a cause, or only things that begin to exist?"

label: Atheist · objection
title: "I'm not 100% sure. I have doubts."
text: Faith isn't intellectual perfection. Jesus welcomes doubters who come to Him. "Do you believe Christ died for your sins and rose again? Will you turn from your sin and trust Him as Lord?" (A caller came to Christ live this way.)

label: Atheist · objection
title: "There's no evidence for God."
text: Creation itself is the evidence: a universe that began, runs on laws, and holds minds and morals. And God gave proof to all by raising Jesus from the dead. "What evidence would you accept?"

label: Atheist · objection
title: "Science has disproved God."
text: Science studies how creation works. It depends on order and laws it cannot explain, and it cannot tell you why anything exists or what is right. "Which experiment showed there is no God?"

label: Atheist · objection
title: "If God is good, why is there so much evil and suffering?"
text: Calling something evil assumes a real standard of good. Scripture names the cause (the fall), shows God turning evil to good, entering suffering at the cross, and promising to end it. "By what standard do you call it evil?"

label: Atheist · objection
title: "The Bible was written by men and is full of errors."
text: Men wrote as they were moved by the Holy Spirit. Ask for a specific error and read it together. "Which error? Let's look at it."

label: Atheist · objection
title: "The God of the Old Testament is a moral monster."
text: To judge Him you need an objective standard, which only He supplies. He judged wicked nations after centuries of patience, He takes no pleasure in the death of the wicked, and He bore judgment Himself at the cross. "If there is no God, what makes anything objectively wrong?"

label: Atheist · objection
title: "Religion causes wars, and Christians are hypocrites."
text: People sin, which is exactly what the Bible says. Jesus condemned hypocrisy harder than anyone. Judge Christianity by Christ. "Does a counterfeit bill prove there's no real money?"

label: Atheist · objection
title: "I'm a good person. I don't need God."
text: Good by whose standard? By God's law, none is righteous, and breaking one point makes us guilty of all. Then give the gospel: Christ died for sinners. "Have you ever lied, stolen, or hated someone? What does that make you before a perfect Judge?"

label: Atheist · objection
title: "Evolution explains life. We don't need a Creator."
text: Change in living things doesn't explain the first life, the information inside it, or the universe it lives in. And Scripture says God made everything in six days and made man directly, in His image. We are not the product of evolution. "Where did the first life, and the information in it, come from?"

label: Atheist · objection
title: "Miracles are impossible."
text: Only if there is no God, which assumes the answer. If God made the universe, raising a man is not hard for Him. "If God created everything, is a resurrection too hard for Him?"

label: Atheist · objection
title: "What about people who have never heard?"
text: Everyone has creation and conscience, and everyone suppresses them. No one is condemned for not hearing, but for sin. The Judge of all the earth will do right. And you have heard. "You've heard. What will you do with Jesus?"

label: Atheist · objection
title: "Faith is believing without evidence."
text: Biblical faith is trust in a Person on good grounds: eyewitness testimony and many convincing proofs. "Do you trust anyone on the basis of testimony?"

label: Atheist · objection
title: "Jesus never existed."
text: Paul received the resurrection report within a few years and met Peter and James, the Lord's brother, in person. "Who did Paul meet in Galatians 1:18–19?"

label: Atheist · quick card
title: "Are you claiming God doesn't exist, or that you don't know?" (Sets the burden.)

label: Atheist · quick card
title: "Have you ever seen something this ordered come from something non-intelligent?"

label: Atheist · quick card
title: "Life only comes from life. Where did the first life come from?"

label: Atheist · quick card
title: "No one dies for what they know is a lie." (1 Cor 15:3–8)

label: Atheist · quick card
title: "If heaven and hell were real, wouldn't you want to know before you die?"

label: Atheist · quick card
title: Rom 1:18–21: they know God and suppress it. Appeal to the conscience, not just the intellect.

label: Holy Spirit · the Spirit is a Person
title: Acts 13:2
text: "Set apart for me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them." First-person speech, a choice, authority. "Do actions have authority, or do persons?" / "He said 'I' and 'me' about Himself. That's self-awareness, right?"

label: Holy Spirit · the Spirit is a Person
title: Acts 15:28
text: "It seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us." He takes part in a decision alongside the apostles. "Can a force agree with a council?"

label: Holy Spirit · the Spirit is a Person
title: Heb 3:7
text: "As the Holy Spirit says…" "Can energy speak to people?"

label: Holy Spirit · the Spirit is a Person
title: Eph 4:30; Isa 63:10; Ps 78:40
text: He can be grieved and rebelled against. "An active force can't be offended. Whoever the Spirit is, He's someone you can offend."

label: Holy Spirit · the Spirit is a Person
title: John 16:13
text: He "does not speak on His own; whatever He hears He speaks." (vs. Oneness or "Spirit = the Father") "Who is the Father hearing from?"

label: Holy Spirit · the Spirit is a Person
title: 1 Cor 1:24
text: Christ is called "the power of God." "Christ is called God's power and He's a person. So being God's power doesn't rule out being a person, right?"

label: Holy Spirit · that Person is Yahweh
title: 2 Sam 23:2–3: "The Spirit of Yahweh speaks by me… the God of Israel has said"
text: Acts 4:24–25: the "Sovereign Lord… who by the Holy Spirit, through the mouth of David" Go-to question: "So the Sovereign Lord who spoke through David is who?"

label: Holy Spirit · that Person is Yahweh
title: Ps 95:7–11: "They tested Me… I swore in My wrath" (Yahweh speaking)
text: Heb 3:7–11: "As the Holy Spirit says… they tested Me… I swore in My wrath" "Who is the Spirit talking about when He says 'they provoked Me'?"

label: Holy Spirit · that Person is Yahweh
title: Isa 6:8–10: the voice of the Lord (Yahweh of hosts, v.3–5) says "Go, and say to this people…"
text: Acts 28:25–26: "The Holy Spirit was right in saying to your fathers through Isaiah, 'Go to this people…'" Also John 12:41: Isaiah saw Christ's glory. One vision, three Persons.

label: Holy Spirit · that Person is Yahweh
title: Jer 31:31–34: "This is the covenant I will make… declares Yahweh"
text: Heb 10:15–17: "The Holy Spirit also bears witness… 'This is the covenant I will make'" The Spirit speaks Yahweh's covenant in the first person.

label: Holy Spirit · that Person is Yahweh
title: Ex 17:7: Israel "tested Yahweh"
text: Heb 3:7–9 (above) Same event.

label: Holy Spirit · that Person is Yahweh
title: Acts 5:3–4: "lie to the Holy Spirit" = "you have not lied to men but to God"
text: One-verse version.

label: Holy Spirit · that Person is Yahweh
title: Rom 8:9; 1 Pet 1:10–11
text: The Spirit is the "Spirit of God" and the "Spirit of Christ" If the Spirit is Yahweh's own Spirit and also Christ's…

label: Holy Spirit · if they say
title: "That's personification."
text: "I didn't ask about figurative language. Can He speak, yes or no? If I say 'my car told me it's not starting today,' did my car speak?". Then: personified wisdom never chooses missionaries in real time (Acts 13:2).

label: Holy Spirit · if they say
title: "He just communicates information / He has no mouth."
text: "Does the Father have a mouth? Does the Father speak?"

label: Holy Spirit · if they say
title: "The Father told the Spirit to say it."
text: The text says "for me… I have called." That's not quoting someone else.

label: Holy Spirit · if they say
title: "He's rational energy, like AI."
text: AI is programmed. The Spirit wills, commands and is provoked. "Can energy be rational without personhood?"

label: Holy Spirit · if they say
title: "God used the Spirit's power to create."
text: God also created through Christ (John 1:3), and Christ is a person.

label: Holy Spirit · if they say
title: "The 'Spirit of Yahweh' means 'from Yahweh,' not 'is Yahweh.'"
text: "The answer is yes to all of them." From Yahweh, and also Yahweh. Not either/or. Then: "He's also the Spirit of Christ, right?" (Rom 8:9). If they deny it, read the verse.

label: Holy Spirit · if they say
title: "OK, so the Spirit is just the Father."
text: John 16:13 (He hears from another), John 14:16 (another Helper whom the Father sends). "Then the Father sends Himself and listens to Himself?"

label: Holy Spirit · if they say
title: They admit it but leave the Bible (an ex-JW who became Muslim because "the Bible says the Spirit is God")
text: that's 2 Tim 4:3, "itching ears." He's conceding the Bible teaches it.

label: Method
title: Phase 1 = agree on the plain text. Nothing else moves until they do.
text: He reads the verse and asks a yes/no question about what it says (not what it means). He won't go on until they answer. "I'm not moving to Phase 2 until you answer Phase 1."

label: Method
title: Yes/no questions, one at a time.
text: "Does the Holy Spirit speak? Yes or no?" Short questions are hard to wriggle out of. Long statements give them room to filibuster.

label: Method
title: Call out the dodge out loud.
text: When they redefine a word ("personification," "communicates information," "a vibe"), he names it: "I didn't ask about personification. I asked, can He speak?"

label: Method
title: Use their rule on another verse.
text: When they invent a rule for one verse (e.g. "no article = 'a god'"), apply the same rule somewhere it obviously fails (John 1:6 becomes "a man sent from a god named a John").

label: Method
title: Hold them to their own analogy.
text: If they bring an analogy (king and messenger, software coder, three judges), don't swap it out. Push it until it proves your point: "Can the agent of the king claim to BE the king?"

label: Method
title: No topic-hopping.
text: When they're losing, they'll jump to "Is Jesus God?" or "the Trinity makes no sense." Don't follow. "You're not going to 'is Jesus God' your way out of this. Defend your claim first."

label: Method
title: Name the goalpost shift.
text: "First you wanted a Bible verse. I gave you the verse. Now it has to come from Jesus' own mouth?"

label: Method
title: "What's the only thing we do? Read."
text: When they say "context," make them show the verse in the context. Then wait. Silence works for you.

label: Method
title: Ask the question back.
text: End with a question they have to answer on their own ("Who is the Father hearing from?"), not a speech.

label: Method
title: Stay warm.
text: Even when they rage-quit: "I want you to be saved, brother. I love you." Truth with love keeps the door open (1 Pet 3:15–16).

label: Method · universal tool
title: "Yahweh" isn't one-person-only.
text: "Yahweh" can name the one divine nature, or any one of the Persons. Their "then Jesus is his own Father" syllogism only works if Yahweh = the Father alone. Show them "Judah" can mean a man or a tribe (Judges 1:1–2).

label: Method · universal tool
title: Word–concept fallacy.
text: "'Trinity' isn't in the Bible" → neither are "monotheism" or "Bible." The question is whether the concept is there.

label: Method · universal tool
title: Three in one way, one in another.
text: Not a contradiction. Different categories: 3 persons, 1 being. (For Muslims, hold up the Hafs, Warsh and Qalun Qurans.)

label: Method · universal tool
title: Context decides literal vs. figurative.
text: Both sides agree personification exists. But personified things don't say "set apart for me" or "the work I have called them to."

label: Method · universal tool
title: "Firstborn" = rank, not birth order.
text: David was the youngest son and the second king, yet God calls him "firstborn, the highest of the kings of the earth" (Ps 89:27).

label: For any conversation
title: The Gospel
text: Every conversation is headed here. Winning the argument saves no one. Christ does. Say the whole message plainly, call for a response, and leave the results to God.

label: The Gospel · Before you speak
title: God saves; you are faithful
text: your job is to say the truth clearly. God gives the growth. (1 Cor 3:6–7; Rom 1:16; John 6:44)

label: The Gospel · Before you speak
title: Law before grace
text: a person has to see their sin and God's judgment before the cross makes sense to them. (Rom 3:19–20; Gal 3:24)

label: The Gospel · Before you speak
title: Jesus is Lord
text: the call is to repent and follow Christ, not to repeat a prayer or add Jesus to a life that stays the same. (Luke 9:23; Rom 10:9; Acts 20:21)

label: The Gospel · Before you speak
title: No false promises
text: the gospel offers forgiveness and Christ Himself, not health, wealth or an easier life. (Phil 3:8; Mark 8:36; 2 Tim 3:12)

label: The Gospel
title: God is holy
text: God created all things and made us for Himself. He is holy and just, He cannot overlook sin, and He will judge every person. (Gen 1:1; Isa 6:3; Hab 1:13; Acts 17:24–31; Heb 9:27) "What do you think happens after we die?"

label: The Gospel
title: We are sinners under judgment
text: Every one of us has broken God's law. We are not basically good people who slip up; we are dead in sin, and the wages of sin is death. No amount of good works can pay it off. (Rom 3:10–12; Rom 3:23; Rom 6:23; Eph 2:1–3; Isa 64:6) "Have you kept God's law perfectly?"

label: The Gospel
title: Christ died and rose
text: God the Son became man, lived the sinless life we have not lived, and died in the place of sinners, bearing the wrath they deserve. He was buried, rose bodily on the third day, and is Lord of all. (John 1:14; Isa 53:5–6; 2 Cor 5:21; 1 Pet 3:18; Rom 5:8; 1 Cor 15:3–4; Phil 2:9–11) "Why did Jesus have to die?"

label: The Gospel
title: Repent and believe
text: God commands all people everywhere to repent. Whoever turns from sin and trusts in Christ alone is forgiven and has eternal life: by grace, through faith, not by works. Following Him costs everything, and no one who comes to Him is turned away. (Mark 1:15; Acts 17:30; John 3:16; Eph 2:8–9; Rom 10:9–13; Luke 14:27–28; John 6:37) "What is keeping you from turning to Christ today?"

label: The Gospel
title: The short version: the Romans Road
text: When you only have a minute, walk these in order. (Rom 3:23; Rom 6:23; Rom 5:8; Rom 10:9–10; Rom 10:13; Rom 8:1)

label: The Gospel
title: How to walk someone through it
text: For a step-by-step way to do this in a real conversation, using the Ten Commandments first and then the cross, open The Way of the Master.

label: The Gospel
title: If they respond
text: Pray with them. Get them a Bible and get them into a church that preaches it, where they can be baptized as a believer. Follow up. (Acts 2:41–42; Matt 28:19–20)

label: The Gospel
title: If they don't
text: Stay warm and leave the door open. You plant and water; God gives the growth. (1 Cor 3:6–7; 1 Pet 3:15–16; 2 Tim 2:24–26)

label: For any conversation
title: The Way of the Master
text: Use the law to reach the conscience, then give the gospel. God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble (James 4:6), so: law to the proud, grace to the humble. The Ten Commandments work like a mirror: they show a person their sin so that the cross makes sense. Jesus did this with the rich young ruler. (Rom 3:19–20; Rom 7:7; Gal 3:24; Mark 10:17–22)

label: The Way of the Master
title: 1. Start with an everyday question
text: Move from ordinary talk to spiritual things with one question. "What do you think happens after we die?"

label: The Way of the Master
title: 2. Are you a good person?
text: Almost everyone says yes. Let them say it. (Prov 20:6) "Would you consider yourself a good person?"

label: The Way of the Master
title: 3. Have you kept the Ten Commandments?
text: Walk through a few, one at a time, and let them answer each. (Ex 20:1–17) "Have you ever told a lie? What does that make you?" "Have you ever taken anything that wasn't yours, whatever its value?" "Have you ever used God's name as a curse word?" Jesus said that looking with lust is adultery in the heart. "Have you ever done that?" (Matt 5:27–28) Jesus put anger under the command "You shall not murder" (Matt 5:21–22), and John says whoever hates his brother is a murderer (1 John 3:15).

label: The Way of the Master
title: 4. Judgment: innocent or guilty?
text: Sum up what they admitted in their own words, then ask. (Heb 9:27; Rom 2:15–16; James 2:10) "If God judges you by that standard, will you be innocent or guilty?"

label: The Way of the Master
title: 5. Destiny: heaven or hell?
text: Don't soften it, and don't gloat. Say it because you care where they end up. (Rev 21:8; 1 Cor 6:9–10) "Would that be heaven or hell? Does that concern you?"

label: The Way of the Master
title: 6. Now give the good news
text: You stand guilty in God's courtroom, and Someone steps in and pays your fine in full. That is what Christ did on the cross, and He rose from the dead. (Rom 5:8; 2 Cor 5:21; 1 Pet 2:24; 1 Cor 15:3–4)

label: The Way of the Master
title: 7. Repent and trust
text: Believing a parachute exists won't save you; you have to put it on. Turn from sin and put your trust in Christ alone, today. (Acts 3:19; Acts 20:21; Rom 13:14; 2 Cor 6:2) "When are you going to do that?"

label: The Way of the Master
title: Keep in mind
text: Already humble? If someone is broken over their sin, skip the law and go straight to grace. answering objections clears the path, but the law and the gospel do the work. Don't spend an hour on arguments and never get here. (Rom 2:15) kind, patient, and plainly concerned for them. (2 Tim 2:24–26) Then go back to The Gospel for the full message and what to do when they respond.

label: For any conversation
title: The Trinity
text: One God in three Persons. One Being, three Persons: the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. One what, three who's. Each line below is taught in Scripture; the Trinity is what you get when you believe all of them at once.

label: The Trinity
title: There is one God
text: (Deut 6:4; Isa 43:10; Isa 44:6; 1 Cor 8:4; James 2:19)

label: The Trinity
title: The Son is God
text: (John 1:1; John 8:58; John 20:28; Col 2:9; Titus 2:13; Heb 1:8)

label: The Trinity
title: The Holy Spirit is God
text: (Acts 5:3–4; 1 Cor 3:16; Ps 139:7–8; Heb 3:7–11) For the full argument, open The Holy Spirit play.

label: The Trinity
title: The three are distinct Persons
text: The Father sends the Son, the Son prays to the Father, and the Spirit is sent by both. All three are present at Jesus' baptism. (Matt 3:16–17; Matt 28:19; John 14:16–17; John 15:26; John 17:5; Gal 4:4–6; 2 Cor 13:14)

label: The Trinity
title: What it is not
text: that is tritheism. Scripture says there is one God. that is modalism. The Father, Son and Spirit speak to and about one another. that is Arianism. All things were made through the Son (John 1:3). "Which of these lines do you disagree with? Let's read the verses for that one."

label: For any conversation
title: Is the Bible reliable?
text: Muslims, Mormons and atheists all attack this from different sides.

label: Is the Bible reliable?
title: We have what they wrote
text: The New Testament survives in thousands of Greek manuscripts, some copied within a few generations of the originals. The Dead Sea Scrolls, copied before and around the time of Christ, match the Hebrew manuscripts copied a thousand years later. (Isa 40:8; Matt 24:35; 1 Pet 1:24–25)

label: Is the Bible reliable?
title: It comes from eyewitnesses
text: The writers were eyewitnesses or wrote down what eyewitnesses told them, while many witnesses were still alive to object. (Luke 1:1–4; 2 Pet 1:16; 1 John 1:1–3; 1 Cor 15:3–8)

label: Is the Bible reliable?
title: Jesus treated Scripture as God's word
text: He quoted it as final, said it cannot be broken, and said every part of it would be fulfilled. (Matt 4:4; Matt 5:17–18; John 10:35; Luke 24:44)

label: Is the Bible reliable?
title: God breathed it out
text: Men spoke from God as they were carried along by the Holy Spirit, so the Scriptures as first written are without error. (2 Tim 3:16–17; 2 Pet 1:20–21)

label: Is the Bible reliable?
title: Prophecy written centuries ahead
text: The suffering Servant, the pierced hands and feet, the birthplace of the Messiah and the pierced One were all written long before Jesus was born. (Isa 53; Ps 22; Mic 5:2; Zech 12:10)

label: Is the Bible reliable?
title: Where to go next
text: run The Islamic Dilemma. The Quran confirms the Scriptures Christians already had. see "translated correctly" under Mormon objections. see "written by men" under Atheist objections. "Which part do you think was changed, and which manuscript shows the change?"

label: For any conversation
title: Words they use
text: A quick lookup for terms that come up in conversation.

label: Words they use · Jehovah's Witness
title: Jehovah
text: their preferred form of God's name (YHWH). For them it names the Father only.

label: Words they use · Jehovah's Witness
title: New World Translation (NWT)
text: the Watchtower's own Bible translation.

label: Words they use · Jehovah's Witness
title: Watchtower / Governing Body
text: the leadership that directs all Witness teaching and calls itself the "faithful and discreet slave."

label: Words they use · Jehovah's Witness
title: Active force
text: their term for the Holy Spirit, whom they say is not a person.

label: Words they use · Jehovah's Witness
title: Kingdom Interlinear
text: the Watchtower's own Greek and English New Testament. Useful because it prints the Greek with a word-for-word English line next to their NWT.

label: Words they use · Jehovah's Witness
title: The 144,000
text: the "anointed" who they say go to heaven. Everyone else hopes for life on a paradise earth.

label: Words they use · Unitarian
title: Biblical Unitarian
text: holds that God is one person, the Father, and Jesus is a human Messiah.

label: Words they use · Unitarian
title: Arian
text: holds that the Son is God's first and greatest creature.

label: Words they use · Unitarian
title: Shaliach (agency)
text: the Jewish idea that a sent agent stands for the one who sent him. They use it to explain away texts where Jesus speaks as God.

label: Words they use · Unitarian
title: Oneness / modalism
text: God is one Person who shows Himself as Father, Son and Spirit (as roles or modes, not three Persons). Oneness Pentecostals say that one Person is Jesus.

label: Words they use · Unitarian
title: Homoousios
text: "of the same essence," the Nicene term for the Son's relation to the Father.

label: Words they use · Unitarian
title: Malak / angelos
text: Hebrew and Greek for "messenger." It names a job, not a nature.

label: Words they use · Mormon
title: Godhead
text: for them, three separate beings who are one in purpose.

label: Words they use · Mormon
title: Exaltation
text: the teaching that faithful people can become gods.

label: Words they use · Mormon
title: Great Apostasy
text: their claim that the true church was lost after the apostles.

label: Words they use · Mormon
title: Restoration
text: their claim that Joseph Smith restored the church.

label: Words they use · Mormon
title: Standard works
text: their four books of scripture: the Bible, the Book of Mormon, the Doctrine and Covenants (D&C), and the Pearl of Great Price.

label: Words they use · Mormon
title: JST
text: the Joseph Smith Translation, his revision of the Bible.

label: Words they use · Mormon
title: Testimony / burning in the bosom
text: an inner feeling taken as God's confirmation that the church is true.

label: Words they use · Mormon
title: King Follett discourse
text: Joseph Smith's 1844 sermon teaching that God was once a man.

label: Words they use · Muslim
title: Tawhid
text: the absolute oneness of Allah.

label: Words they use · Muslim
title: Shirk
text: associating anything with Allah. The one sin Allah will not forgive if a person dies in it (Q 4:48).

label: Words they use · Muslim
title: Isa
text: the Quran's name for Jesus.

label: Words they use · Muslim
title: Tawrat, Zabur, Injil
text: the Torah, the Psalms and the Gospel, which the Quran says Allah revealed.

label: Words they use · Muslim
title: Tahrif
text: the claim that the earlier Scriptures were corrupted.

label: Words they use · Muslim
title: Hadith
text: reports of what Muhammad said and did.

label: Words they use · Muslim
title: Surah / ayah
text: a chapter and a verse of the Quran.

label: Words they use · Muslim
title: Tafsir
text: commentary on the Quran.

label: Words they use · Muslim
title: Hafs, Warsh, Qalun
text: different transmitted readings of the Quran.

label: Words they use · Atheist
title: Atheist
text: does not believe in God. Some go further and say there is no God.

label: Words they use · Atheist
title: Agnostic
text: says they don't know, or that no one can know.

label: Words they use · Atheist
title: Naturalism
text: the view that nature is all there is.

label: Words they use · Atheist
title: Objective morality
text: right and wrong that are true whatever anyone thinks.

label: Words they use · Atheist
title: Burden of proof
text: whoever makes a claim has to back it up. "There is no God" is a claim.

label: Words they use · Words we use
title: Trinity
text: one God in three Persons. See The Trinity.

label: Words they use · Words we use
title: Two natures
text: Jesus is one Person who is truly God and truly man.

label: Words they use · Words we use
title: Monogenes
text: Greek for "one of a kind," often translated "only begotten."

label: Words they use · Words we use
title: Prototokos
text: Greek for "firstborn." In texts like Col 1:15 (cf. Ps 89:27) it means the preeminent heir, not the first one created.

label: Words they use · Words we use
title: Arche
text: Greek for "beginning," "origin" or "ruler."
